# Loophole

> Loophole is a free, open-source (MIT) static security scanner that ships as a single Python file with zero dependencies. It scans JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Go and PHP code for security flaws, explains why each finding matters in plain English, and suggests a concrete fix for every finding.

## What it does

- 61 security checks: hardcoded secrets and passwords, SQL / NoSQL / LDAP injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), command injection, eval() code injection, SSRF, prototype pollution, unsafe deserialization, XML external entity (XXE), open redirects, Zip Slip, unsafe file uploads, missing CSRF protection, ReDoS, JWT weaknesses ('none' algorithm, weak secrets, unverified tokens), outdated TLS versions and disabled TLS verification, weak crypto (MD5/SHA-1 password hashing, DES/RC4, hardcoded or zero IVs, ECB mode), predictable random values, secrets written to logs, missing security headers, debug mode and error-detail leaks. v1.1.0 adds 11 more: server-side template injection (SSTI), cookies set without HttpOnly, weak PHP randomness (rand/mt_rand/uniqid) for tokens, TLS validation disabled via ssl.CERT_NONE / unverified contexts / NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, CORS reflecting any Origin or credentials with a wildcard origin, HTTP header injection (response splitting), non-constant-time secret comparison, DOM open redirects, libxmljs entity expansion, framework HTML sinks (insertAdjacentHTML, Vue v-html, Angular bypassSecurityTrust), and jsonpickle / v8 deserialization.
- Lightweight taint tracking: follows user input from source (request data, form fields, superglobals) to dangerous sinks (queries, shells, HTML output), so findings are real data flows, not keyword noise.
- Runs fully offline, in seconds, with no account and no telemetry; an optional `.loophole.json` config file (exclude paths, disable rules, severity overrides), `loophole:ignore` inline suppressions, `--baseline` / `--write-baseline`, and `--html` reports are available. Python 3.8+ standard library only.
- Official GitHub Action (rootsiemen/loophole@v1) runs it on every push and pull request and uploads SARIF results to the repository Security tab.
- Loophole Server Guard — the runtime tool in the same project: it watches a live server's web (Apache/Nginx) and SSH/auth logs in real time, scores every IP's behaviour, and alerts (terminal, email, Telegram or webhook) with the attacker's IP; IPs that cross the ban threshold are banned at the firewall (iptables, nft or ufw) with an expiry, a whitelist that can never be banned, and dry-run enabled by default. Decoy honeypot ports (fake SSH, fake WordPress/phpMyAdmin logins, a fake .env) catch probers, incidents persist in a SQLite store, and a local dashboard shows top attackers, active bans and recent incidents. Server Guard also runs Loophole's own code scans against the server's code on a schedule — new critical/high findings raise the same alarm, so code holes and live attacks appear in one dashboard. Pure Python 3 standard library, zero dependencies.
- Exit code 1 on critical/high findings, so CI fails exactly when it should; `--fix-dry` prints suggested patches as diffs without modifying files.
